correctness.rationale: For Im(z)>0, theta(t)=arg(z+t) decreases on [a,b]. Outside the disk, theta(a)-theta(b)<pi/2, so the order-two kernel values span an angle strictly less than pi and a rotation makes their real parts positive; a nonzero positive measure cannot integrate them to zero. Real points outside the cut give a positive integrand, and the lower half-plane follows by conjugation. Inside the disk, the intermediate value theorem selects t* with theta(a)-theta(t*)=pi/2; masses |z+a|^2 and |z+t*|^2 make the two terms opposite unit phases. The exact examples at support [0,1] verify boundary and interior sharpness.
